description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the loss ratio (%) and the number of TFLOPs for different models, including Vanilla, SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=128), SepLLM (n=64, H), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T). The x-axis represents the number of TFLOPs on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 1e7 to 9e8, with labeled tick marks at 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 3e8, 4e8, 5e8, 6e8, 7e8, 8e8, and 9e8. The y-axis shows the loss ratio in percentage, ranging from 94% to 100%, with grid lines at 95%, 96%, 97%, 98%, 99%, and 100%. The Vanilla model is represented by a purple line with triangle markers, which remains relatively stable around 99.8% across all TFLOP values. The SepLLM (n=64) model, shown in orange with square markers, starts at approximately 98.1% and increases to around 100% before slightly declining. The SepLLM (n=128) model, in blue with cross markers, begins at 97.2% and rises to about 99.8%, showing a similar trend to the Vanilla model. The SepLLM (n=64, H) model, depicted in green with diamond markers, starts at 97.5% and increases to approximately 100%, maintaining a high loss ratio. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model, shown in red with circle markers, starts at 94% and increases sharply to around 99%, then fluctuates slightly around 98.8% as TFLOPs increase.
